verses.english: The Interior as Impermanent in the Three Times
“Mendicants, the eye of the past and future is impermanent,

verses.pali: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītasmiṁ cakkhusmiṁ anapekkho hoti;
verses.english: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple is not concerned with the eye of the past,
they don’t look forward to enjoying the eye in the future,

verses.pali: paccuppannassa cakkhussa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: and they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the eye in the present.

verses.pali: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītāya jivhāya anapekkho hoti;
paccuppannāya jivhāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.

verses.english: mind of the past and future is impermanent,

verses.pali: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītasmiṁ manasmiṁ anapekkho hoti;
verses.english: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple doesn’t worry about the mind of the past,
they don’t look forward to enjoying the mind in the future,

verses.pali: paccuppannassa manassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hotī”ti.
verses.english: and they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the mind in the present.”
